target_claim: The proof asserts that the dual of the meet-prime condition is the displayed formula on line 0007, and then that this displayed formula is exactly the definition of 'z is a join prime element'. As written, the displayed formula has 'z \preceq z' as its first disjunct (instead of 'z \preceq x'), so it is vacuously true by reflexivity for every element z of every ordered set, and therefore is NOT equivalent to join primeness.
source_quote: :$\forall x, y \in S: \paren{z \preceq x \vee y} \implies \leftparen{z \preceq z}$ or $\rightparen{z \preceq y}$
